content: MED1, also referred to as DRIP205 or Trap220, is a subunit of the Mediator complex and is encoded by the MED1 gene in humans. This protein functions as a nuclear receptor coactivator. The process of gene transcription activation involves multiple steps and is initiated by factors that recognize transcriptional enhancer sites within DNA. These factors collaborate with coactivators to facilitate the initiation of transcription by the RNA polymerase II machinery. MED1 is a subunit of the CRSP (cofactor required for SP1 activation) complex, which, along with TFIID, is necessary for efficient activation by SP1. Additionally, MED1 is a component of other multisubunit complexes. It plays a regulatory role in p53-dependent apoptosis and is critical for adipogenesis. Furthermore, MED1 has the capacity to self-oligomerize. MED1 has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins and receptors, including the androgen receptor, BRCA1, calcitriol receptor, cyclin-dependent kinase 8, estrogen receptor alpha, glucocorticoid receptor, hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha, p53, PPARGC1A, PPARG, TGS1, and thyroid hormone receptor alpha. This protein is part of the Mediator complex and specifically represents the subunit Med1. It is a component of the Med9 submodule within the Srb/Med complex. MED1 is one of three subunits essential for the viability of the entire organism, as it plays a pivotal role in environmentally-directed cell-fate decisions.
